title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The surrounding pages study the 'équation des lacets', i.e. the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type cocycle equations for elements g, g_0, h_0, ξ, λ_0, λ of π̂_{0,3} (the profinite free group on two generators, the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}). These equations are taken under the order-3 automorphism ρ that cyclically permutes 0, 1, ∞. Section (VII) pushes these equations down to a small quotient where explicit matrix computation is possible. The free group π_{0,3} is identified with Γ(2)/±1 inside PSL(2,Z). Its congruence completion (written π(2)'^c) maps into PSL(2,Ẑ) = SL(2,Ẑ)/±1. Grothendieck works more generally in GL(2,Ẑ)/±1.

Identifying ρ. From the formulas one recovers ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]]. It satisfies ρ^3 = -1, so it has order 3 in PSL and normalises Γ(2). The automorphism ρ acts by conjugation: ρ(g) = ρ g ρ^{-1}, and ρ^2(g) = ρ^{-1} g ρ.

Formulas (77). For g = [[a,b],[c,d]] with δ = det g:
- ρ(g) = [[c+d, -c], [c+d-a-b, a-c]];
- ρ^2(g) = [[d-b, a+b-c-d], [-b, a+b]];
- δ ρ(g^{-1}) and δ ρ^2(g^{-1}) are obtained by applying these to the adjugate [[d,-b],[-c,a]].

Formula (78). The commutator [g,ρ] = gρg^{-1}ρ^{-1} = [[A,B],[C,D]] has
- δA = (a²+ab+b²) - (ac+bd+bc), δB = ac+bd+bc,
- δC = -(c²+cd+d²) + (ac+ad+bd), δD = c²+cd+d²,
- hence C + D - B = 1 (the marginal NB).

The cocycle equation. Grothendieck then rewrites the cocycle equation (79), g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = 1, as g ρ(g) = ρ^{-1}(g^{-1}) and sets gρ(g) = [[P,Q],[R,S]]. The next page computes P = (a+b)(c+d-b), Q = -a(c-b) - bc, R = (c+d)² - d(a+b), S = ad - c(c+d). It then solves prime by prime in PSL(2,Z_ℓ), splitting into the cases a+b ≠ 0 (giving c+d-b = 1/δ and δ³ = 1) and a+b = 0.

Purpose. The aim is to test whether the many necessary conditions Grothendieck derived for Galois-type elements are automatically satisfied, by computing in this 'tiny' quotient. The margin says these are calculations 'par acquit de conscience, ne serviront peut-être plus!'.

Modern reading. Since (gρ)^3 = gρ(g)ρ²(g)ρ^3 and ρ^3 = ±1, the cocycle equation says exactly that gρ has order dividing 3 in PSL. For det 1 this means:
- either tr(gρ) = c+d-b = ±1,
- or gρ = ±1, i.e. g = ρ^{-1}.

This matches and simplifies the case analysis on the next page: the a+b = 0 branch reduces to g = ρ^{-1}, or to b a primitive cube root of unity, which again gives c+d-b = 1.
errors: No errors on this page: all of (77) and (78) check out with ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]], and the NB C+D-B = 1 is correct.
The marginal NB is written ambiguously (C+D-B = ... δ = det g = ad-bc); the correct statement is C+D-B = 1, equivalently δ(C+D-B) = δ.

The computation chosen (sign-by-sign matrix comparison) is heavier than needed. The equation is equivalent to (gρ)^3 = ±1, i.e. tr(gρ) = c+d-b = ±1 or g = ρ^{-1}. The next page's case a+b = 0 compares R = (c+d)² with δ²/b² instead of with the (2,1) entry b of ρ²(g^{-1}). This slip does not affect the final classification.

ideas.what: Projecting the loop/cocycle equations (GT-type relations under the order-3 symmetry ρ of P^1 minus 3 points) to the congruence quotient PSL(2,Ẑ) of the free profinite group, to obtain explicitly computable necessary conditions
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT / Galois cocycles in the congruence completion of Γ(2) ≅ F_2; congruence quotient of F̂_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto and related work on Galois action on modular/congruence completions (general circle of ideas)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Ŝl(2,Z) and the Teichmüller tower in general terms; these explicit computations are not published as far as I know

ideas.what: Explicit matrix formulas for the action of the order-3 automorphism ρ and for the commutator [g,ρ] in GL(2)
ideas.modern_name: Conjugation by the order-3 element [[0,1],[-1,1]] normalising Γ(2)

ideas.what: Solving the 3-cocycle equation gρ(g)ρ²(g) = 1 in PSL(2,Z_ℓ) prime by prime
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian 1-cocycles of Z/3 acting on PSL(2,Z_ℓ); equivalently, elements of order 3 in the coset PSL·ρ

deep.surprise_reason: Routine, correct matrix bookkeeping projecting the GT-type cocycle equation to PSL(2,Ẑ). Grothendieck himself flags it as possibly useless, and the classification follows trivially from the trace criterion for order 3. It is of mild historical interest only, as evidence that he tested the loop equations on congruence quotients.
transcription_corrections: Title: 'Calculs dans Sl(2,Ẑ)' = Sl(2,Ẑ)/±1' (the prime denotes the quotient by ±1), rather than a hatted Sl on the left.
The list of letters reads 'g, g_0, h_0, ξ, λ_0, λ' (matching the previous page); the uncertain 'ρ_1 [?]' should be ξ.
'(ou dans Gl(2,Ẑ)' ≃ Gl(2,Ẑ)/±1)' – the image reads Gl on both sides, not Sl.
Marginal NB: 'C+D-B = 1', with 'δ = det g = ad-bc' written below.
The margin at top left reads 'Calculs "par acquit de conscience", ne serviront peut-être plus!'.
